meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: The ideal start to the day is an invigorating shower.

examples.text: Плотный завтрак и чашечка горячего кофе.
examples.trans: A hearty breakfast and a little cup of hot coffee.
Ouch, Lyova, that is very hot!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я понимаю, у меня нет шансов.
examples.trans: I understand, I do not have a chance.

examples.text: Ты должен мне помочь с Катей.
examples.trans: You have to help me with Katya.
What? I am not going to help.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'can, am able to', paired with 'смочь'.

examples.text: Ты должен мне помочь с Катей.
examples.trans: You have to help me with Katya.
I can't today.
That can't be.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'their', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я понимаю, у меня нет шансов.
examples.trans: I understand, I do not have a chance.
Come on, why are you writing yourself off?

examples.text: А они вон какие разные люди.
examples.trans: And look how different those two people are.

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to take', paired with 'брать'.

examples.text: Дима, я не могу их взять.
examples.trans: Dima, I cannot take them right now.
Go and hire Galileo.
Take the money.

meanings.note: Prefix 'из-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'винить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'sorry', paired with 'извинять'.

examples.text: Извини, но пока я не могу.
examples.trans: Forgive me, but for now I cannot.
Sorry, I'm in a hurry.
Sorry, please.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'but', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: The ideal start to the day is an invigorating shower.
Forgive me, please, I did it by accident.

examples.text: А что, это так заметно, да?
examples.trans: Wait, is it really that noticeable?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'for now', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Всё, мама, пока, мне пора работать.
examples.trans: Alright, Mom, bye, it is time for me to work.

examples.text: Извини, но пока я не могу.
examples.trans: Forgive me, but for now I cannot.
Bye, Dad!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'hello'.

examples.trans: Hello, friends, meet Sveta.
Hello, very nice to meet you, I am Victoria.
Hello, Arkady Borisovich!

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'friend' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: She shies away from all of my friends.
Hello, friends, meet Sveta.

examples.text: А может, мы с ним любим друг друга!
examples.trans: And maybe he and I love each other!

meanings.en: to get acquainted, to meet (someone new)
meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'meet', paired with 'познакомиться'.

examples.trans: Well then, let's get acquainted.
Meet Vika.

examples.text: Очень хорошо. Ну что, давайте знакомиться.
examples.trans: Very good. Well then, let's introduce everyone.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, it (is)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Ouch, Lyova, that is very hot!

examples.text: А что, это так заметно, да?
examples.trans: Wait, is it really that noticeable?
For you this kind of thing is familiar.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'very', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Ouch, Lyova, that is very hot!
It is a question on a very delicate matter.

examples.text: Честно говоря, я сам не знаю почему.
examples.trans: Honestly, I do not know why myself.

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'ятный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('pleasant').

examples.trans: Hello, very nice to meet you, I am Victoria.
Enjoy your meal!
He's a very nice person.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'actor' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Я актёр, поэтому меня все узнают.
examples.trans: I am an actor, so everyone recognizes me.
He is a famous cinema actor.

examples.text: Прямо как знаменитый актёр Стивен Снегов!
examples.trans: Just like the famous actor Steven Snegov!

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'этому').

examples.text: Я актёр, поэтому меня все узнают.
examples.trans: I am an actor, so everyone recognizes me.

examples.text: Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: That's why I'm running for a second term.
I'm tired, so I'm at home.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'all', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Have you completely lost your conscience?
Everything's fine.
As you all know...

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'знать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will know', paired with 'узнавать'.

examples.text: Подожди здесь, я сейчас всё узнаю.
examples.trans: Wait right here, I will go find out everything now.
I just found out something important.

examples.text: Я актёр, поэтому меня все узнают.
examples.trans: I am an actor, so everyone recognizes me.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'let's', paired with 'дать'.

examples.text: Давай поспорим с тобой на зарплату!
examples.trans: Let us bet a month's salary on it!
Let us drink to our acquaintance!
Let's talk.

meanings.en: to drink up, to have a drink
meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'пить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'let's drink', paired with 'выпивать'.

examples.trans: Oh, I've had a bit to drink now.
Drink some water.
May I drink a tiny drop of beer?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'for', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Плотный завтрак и чашечка горячего кофе.
examples.trans: A hearty breakfast and a little cup of hot coffee.

examples.text: Наш Лёва запал на дочку шефа.
examples.trans: Our Lyova has fallen for the Chef's daughter.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'our', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Наш Лёва запал на дочку шефа.
examples.trans: Our Lyova has fallen for the Chef's daughter.

examples.text: Если бы хотел, сразу бы нашёл.
examples.trans: If I wanted one, I would find one right away.

examples.text: Ну что, где будет наше свидание?
examples.trans: So, where is our date going to be?

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'acquaintance, meeting' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Let us drink to our acquaintance!
Our acquaintance started somehow wrong.

examples.text: Костя, я имела в виду знакомство с родителями.
examples.trans: Kostya, I meant meeting the parents.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian expressive spoken interjection meaning 'hello', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: For you this kind of thing is familiar.
Chef, Timur has brought the groceries out there.

examples.text: Привет, Макс, я хотела тебе сказать.
examples.trans: Hi, Max, I wanted to tell you something.

meanings.note: Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'flowers' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Привет, Катя, это цветы для тебя.
examples.trans: Hi, Katya, these flowers are for you.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'for', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: For you this kind of thing is familiar.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'пасибо'). Common neuter noun meaning 'thank you' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Спасибо тебе, что бы я делал?
examples.trans: Thank you, what would I have done without you?
Thank you, that is very sweet, Lyova.

examples.text: Да ты мне ещё спасибо скажешь!
examples.trans: Why, you will thank me for this yet!

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Thank you, that is very sweet, Lyova.
It's very nice here.
She smiled very sweetly.

meanings.en: must, need to, it is necessary
meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: А от меня что тебе надо?
examples.trans: And what do you need from me?
They should put up a monument to Lena.
Alright, I really need to get going.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'nothing', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: К сожалению, ничего у нас не получится.
examples.trans: Unfortunately, nothing will work out for us.

examples.text: Ты главное только не нервничай так.
examples.trans: The main thing is just do not get so nervous.

examples.text: Я вообще ничего теперь не понимаю.
examples.trans: I do not understand anything at all now.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to speak', paired with 'сказать'.

examples.text: Хорошо, договорились, приходи на час позже.
examples.trans: Alright, it is a deal, come an hour later.

examples.text: Хорошо, Макс, мы с тобой договорились.
examples.trans: Alright, Max, we have a deal.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Не всё, что говорят, чистая правда.
examples.trans: Not everything people say is the pure truth.

examples.text: Ты будешь во всём меня слушаться.
examples.trans: You will obey me in everything.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'know'.

examples.text: Честно говоря, я сам не знаю почему.

meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'ождать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'wait', paired with 'ждать'.

examples.trans: Wait, I'll be right there.

examples.text: Подожди, Нин, ты не поняла. Это же стыдно!
examples.trans: Wait, Nina, you don't get it. It's shameful!

examples.trans: Forgive me, please, I did it by accident.

examples.text: Ладно, я попробую устроить вам свидание.
examples.trans: Alright, I will try to arrange a date for you two.

examples.text: Я хотел спросить у тебя совет.
examples.trans: I wanted to ask you for some advice.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'what; what a', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: А они вон какие разные люди.
examples.trans: And look how different those two people are.

examples.text: Посмотри, какой я молодой и поджарый.
examples.trans: Look how young and lean I am.

examples.text: На моей кухне никаких интрижек не потерплю!
examples.trans: I will not tolerate any flings in my kitchen!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'else/more', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Maybe not everything is lost yet?

examples.text: Мы ещё обязательно сходим попьём кофе.
examples.trans: We will definitely go have coffee some time.

examples.text: Стой, подожди, я ещё не договорил.
examples.trans: Stop, wait, I have not finished speaking yet.
